findings.action: After an initial computation declines retention, every waiting caller invokes compute directly and discards its keep flag. If the read recovers, these callers can duplicate successful work concurrently, none publishes its success, and the next caller computes the same successful input again without any eviction. This leaves R1/R2/R3 and R6 unsatisfied. Retry through coordinated cache acquisition so a recovered success is published and shared; cover concurrent failure followed by recovery.

Capacity eviction replaces the entire entries map, including computations whose ready channels have not closed. For example, with bound 1, block computation A, request B to clear the map, then request A again: the second A computes while the original A is still running. All four production caches inherit this violation of R6 at capacity. Preserve in-flight coordination independently of retained-value eviction and cover a capacity crossing while a key is pending.
